mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in WORKPLACES mobility lifts weekday trip chaining and lunch-time shopping, so RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks as commuting activity stays elevated.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -21.9 to -15.1 over the last three weekly means while TRANSIT improved from -11.1 to -7.4
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain less negative for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays above 6 percentage points and WORKPLACES remains below -18, households substitute toward local errands and neighborhood shopping, which raises RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 while WORKPLACES stays below -18
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated and WORKPLACES remaining strongly negative.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers by more than 2 points from one week to the next, access friction falls and shopping trips follow commuting corridors, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -11.1 to -7.4 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: Reject if a week-on-week transit rebound greater than 2 points is not followed by higher RETAIL_REC within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility signals a shift away from discretionary outdoor recreation and toward indoor retail trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -27.4 to -22.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week after a weekly decline of at least 3 points in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: During a steady decline in PARKS and persistent residential time, people reallocate weekend activity from outdoor leisure to malls and stores, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL stays positive across all four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC is not higher after four weeks in periods where PARKS stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 6.

mechanism_narrative: A further rise in GROCERY_PHARM above 20 points indicates concentrated essential errands and nearby foot traffic, which spills over into retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from 12.9 to 22.4 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 20.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, the same-day city-center circulation increases and supports retail demand, so RETAIL_REC moves up over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved between t-3w and t-0w despite weak levels
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over 28 days after simultaneous two-week gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: In late-October festival preparation, stronger grocery and workplace activity converts into shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC rises only in this calendar-season window over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is the strongest positive series in the snapshot and WORKPLACES is still negative but improving on balance
